Commentary.Commentary: That’s all from Abu Dhabi in this year’s Asia Cup, but the action continues in Dubai on Wednesday, 24th September, when India take on Bangladesh. An Indian win will see them through to the final and eliminate Sri Lanka from finals contention even before their last Super Four game, while a Bangladesh victory would keep the island nation alive. If India prevail, it would set up a virtual semi-final on Thursday, 25th September, between Pakistan and Bangladesh. The first ball of the India-Bangladesh game will be bowled at 2.30 pm GMT, with our build-up starting well in advance. Until then, take care and goodbye!

The skipper of Pakistan, Salman Agha, says that he always smiles but can’t call this a perfect game, as they lost four wickets in quick succession. Apart from that, he feels that it was nearly perfect, with the boys stepping up and performing well. Adds that the guys are putting in the hard work, doing extra on the field, and it is clearly paying off. Praises Shaheen Afridi, calling him an asset and a match-winner who has been bowling exceptionally well since the USA tour. On Hussain Talat’s all-round impact, Salman says this is exactly why they back all-rounders, and he is delighted to see him deliver. Speaking about Mohammad Nawaz, the skipper points out his immense batting potential and hopes he continues to show consistency. On Abrar Ahmed, he says that the spinner has been outstanding whenever the team is in a tough spot. He also mentions Abrar’s cheeky celebration mimicking Hasaranga, saying it was all in good spirit, and the two gelled well after the match. Salman concludes by stressing that Abrar is a rare talent and he expects greater things for him in the future.

The captain of Sri Lanka, Charith Asalanka, says that after losing 5 wickets inside the first 10 overs, it was always going to be tough. Mentions that the surface looked really good, and it was not ideal to lose those wickets in the first half. Admits that Pakistan bowled and fielded well in that phase. Shares that he is happy with the fight shown by his team. Praises Wanindu Hasaranga by calling him a superstar of white-ball cricket.

Hussain Talat is adjudged the PLAYER OF THE MATCH for his impressive all-round performance. Says that the team had prepared well for the hot and humid conditions, and he made sure to take his time before playing his shots. Adds that playing in the UAE was something they had discussed in team meetings, and he is pleased to have contributed to the win. Talking about his partnership with Mohammad Nawaz, Talat shares that he was feeling drained due to the humidity and asked Nawaz to go hard at the other end, which worked perfectly. On his bowling, he mentions that he has been working closely with the bowling coach and feels that even if he delivers two good overs for his team, he considers that a success.
Time for the presentation ceremony...

Earlier, after being asked to bat first, Sri Lanka went too hard, too soon. The surface was far better than the 133 they eventually ended up with, but they just did not give themselves time and kept taking risks. Reduced to 58/5 inside the 8th over, and then 80/6, they were in deep trouble. Kamindu Mendis was tasked with arresting the slide, and his partnership with Chamika Karunaratne brought some stability. Mendis’ third T20I half-century gave his bowlers something to work with. For Pakistan, Shaheen Afridi struck twice in the Powerplay, though it came at a cost. The middle overs were bossed by Abrar Ahmed, who conceded just 8 runs from his 4 overs while also picking up a wicket.

Seeing a partnership developing, Charith Asalanka was forced to bring Dushmantha Chameera back into the attack, and he delivered by breaking the flourishing stand. At 80/5 with 54 more needed, Mohammad Nawaz joined Hussain Talat at the crease. Sri Lanka were counting on Wanindu Hasaranga’s two remaining overs, but Nawaz attacked Hasaranga effectively, and Talat followed suit. Those two overs, which Sri Lanka had pinned their hopes on, ended up being expensive and effectively sealed the fate of the game.

In pursuit of 134, Pakistan got off to a brisk start. While Fakhar Zaman looked unsettled after taking a knock on the head, Sahibzada Farhan took charge and eased the early nerves with a flurry of boundaries. At 45/0, things seemed firmly under control before a sudden collapse saw them slip to 57/4 in no time. Given the platform laid by the openers and the modest target, there was no real scoreboard pressure. This chase was always going to be more about handling the nerves than the numbers.

A stutter along the way, but Pakistan get the job done and collect their first points in the Super Four stage. This win snaps their losing streak against the island nation in this format, having lost the previous five meetings. For Sri Lanka, it is now two defeats in a row in the Super Four stage. They are not out of finals contention just yet, but they are not far from it either. The road ahead for Charith Asalanka and his men is looking increasingly steep.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK! It has been an entertaining tussle so far. Pakistan landed the first blow with 43 runs in the first 5 overs without losing a wicket, but the next 5 overs have seen Sri Lanka roar back with 4 quick strikes. Given the strong platform laid by the openers, it is now about batting sensibly and not letting the pressure creep in from Pakistan’s perspective. Sri Lanka, meanwhile, must keep chipping away at the wickets as that remains their best chance of defending the total. Maheesh Theekshana and Wanindu Hasaranga still have two overs each up their sleeve, and those four overs will be absolute gold dust. Charith Asalanka has a decision to make on when to use them. Theekshana (2-0-11-2) returns to the attack.

Commentary.Commentary: Aggression straightaway! Full and around middle, Ayub dances down the track and drives it straight downtown. The ball hits the boot of Fakhar Zaman at the other end and parries away towards mid off. A single taken.

Commentary.Commentary: Saim Ayub walks out to bat.

OUT! TAKEN! GONE! Maheesh Theekshana provides the much-needed breakthrough, and the good cameo of Sahibzada Farhan comes to an end. Too full and wide outside off, Farhan gets down on one knee and throws his hands to reach out. Mistimes his shot off the toe end of the bat, and the ball goes flat towards mid off, where Kamindu Mendis backpedals a bit and takes it over his head. Theekshana roars in delight and celebrates the wickets with his teammates. Pakistan are 45/1, needing 89 runs more in 87 balls.
Commentary.Howout: c Kamindu Mendis b Maheesh Theekshana
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Maheesh Theekshana to Sahibzada Farhan, OUT! c Kamindu Mendis b Maheesh Theekshana.

Commentary.Commentary: Short and around leg, Sahibzada Farhan again backs away and gets down on one knee to sweep but misses. Wears it high on the thigh pad.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Maheesh Theekshana to Sahibzada Farhan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Follows the batter, full and down leg, Sahibzada Farhan backs away and chips it straight downtown over the bowler's head for two runs. The long on fielder cuts it off to his left.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Maheesh Theekshana to Sahibzada Farhan, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: At 138.4 kph, on a short of a good length, over middle. Fakhar gives himself room and carves it over the in-field on the off side for a brace.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Dushmantha Chameera to Fakhar Zaman, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Chameera switches to around the wicket and goes into the wicket, over middle. Fakhar picks the slower one and steers it in front of backward point. Zaman is keen for a single but Farhan sends him back.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Dushmantha Chameera to Fakhar Zaman, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a shortish length, on middle. Fakhar pulls it to the right of deep backward square leg for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Dushmantha Chameera to Fakhar Zaman, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Pace off and going away from the batter, on a back of a length. Zaman drags it off the back foot to the left of the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Dushmantha Chameera to Fakhar Zaman, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good effort in the deep! Chameera bashes the hard length, over middle. Farhan swings it away on the leg side and gets it high on the bat. The ball plugs in the vacant deep mid-wicket region. Kamindu Mendis sprints to his left in the deep and as he flicks the ball away from the fence, the ball catches his trailing leg and drops in front of the boundary cushions. It is mopped up by the fielder converging from the inner circle. Three runs taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Dushmantha Chameera to Sahibzada Farhan, 3 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Big swing and a miss! On a good length, on off and middle. Sahibzada Farhan clears the front leg and has a hack across the line. Fails to connect and the ball goes over the stumps.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Dushmantha Chameera to Sahibzada Farhan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Change of ends for Dushmantha Chameera. Also, Sri Lanka had scored 36 runs after the first four overs, but they had lost two wickets, which could be key in this big contest.

FOUR! That will only rub salt into the wounds! Shorter and fractionally wide on off. Zaman stays on the back foot and cuts it late to thread the gap between backward point and short third for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Maheesh Theekshana to Fakhar Zaman, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: STUMPING CHANCE MISSED! Not an easy one, but Sri Lanka need to convert every chance that comes their way if they want to defend 133! This is fired in by Theekshana, around the leg stump. Fakhar skips down the track and ends up getting too close to the ball. Gets beaten on the outside edge, and the ball bounces once after going past him and in front of the keeper. Kusal Mendis fails to get up, and the ball gets past his right thigh and races away.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Maheesh Theekshana to Fakhar Zaman, 4 Byes.

Commentary.Commentary: Darted into the right-hander, on the fuller side. Sahibzada Farhan has a swipe across the line and the bottom hand comes off the handle. Miscues it in front of deep mid-wicket for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Maheesh Theekshana to Sahibzada Farhan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Theekshana spots the batter backing away and follows him, on a nagging length. Farhan slaps it straight to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Maheesh Theekshana to Sahibzada Farhan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Very full, a bit of air given, on off, firmly driven to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Maheesh Theekshana to Sahibzada Farhan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pushed through at 98.5 kph, full and on the off stump. Fakhar knocks it to the right of mid-wicket for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Maheesh Theekshana to Fakhar Zaman, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Spin time. Maheesh Theekshana is introduced early in the attack in the Powerplay, who often bowls with a new ball.
A well-directed bumper, at the right shoulder of the batter. Sahibzada Farhan ducks and lets the ball go past him. 18 runs off the over!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Nuwan Thushara to Sahibzada Farhan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! All class! Nuwan Thushara rolls his fingers over the ball, on a good length, around the off stump. Farhan extends his hands into the drive and hits it between cover and mid off for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Nuwan Thushara to Sahibzada Farhan, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! More of a slice, but it does the job for Sahibzada Farhan! Thushara hurls it on a length, outside off. Sahibzada clears his front leg and, with a clean extension of the arms, he clears the long off fence for six more.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Nuwan Thushara to Sahibzada Farhan, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Swinging back into the pads, on a length. Zaman makes use of the swing and works it through square leg for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Nuwan Thushara to Fakhar Zaman, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pace off this time at 118.5 kph, on a length, at the stumps. Sahibzada Farhan is early into the drive and mishits it towards long on for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Nuwan Thushara to Sahibzada Farhan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! All the way! This is on a length, a bit of away curve, on off. Due to Nuwan's slingy action, the ball does not rise as much and stays a bit low. Farhan holds his shape and lofts it over mid on for a six.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Nuwan Thushara to Sahibzada Farhan, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: The physio is out again as Fakhar Zaman doesn't seem 100 per cent and appears to be struggling to sight the ball properly. There have been talks between him and the physio, and Zaman has decided to stay for now.

FOUR! Just over! On a back of a length, on middle. Zaman is unable to free his arms in the way he would have wanted, ideally. Swings like a rusty gate but gets enough bat to clear the leaping mid-wicket fielder for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Dushmantha Chameera to Fakhar Zaman, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Swing and a miss this time! Angled away from the southpaw, on a good length. Zaman charges down the track and has a wild swing. Misses by a long way, does Fakhar.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Dushmantha Chameera to Fakhar Zaman, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Beaten! This is served at 143.4 kph, fuller in length. Fakhar is all at sea with his footwork. Just hangs his bat out with no real conviction and the ball nips back to go past the inside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Dushmantha Chameera to Fakhar Zaman, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: The physio is out, and a mandatory concussion test is going on with Fakhar Zaman, who got hit on his helmet on the previous delivery. Seems a big blow, and now, Zaman is taking some refreshment drinks. A blow is pointed by Zaman on his forehead, as it seems there is a cut or something off the grills of the helmet. There is a change of helmet for him, and it looks like a good sign as Fakhar is up on his feet and feels well enough to continue further.

Serious heat from Dushmantha Chameera! Oh, hang on, Sri Lanka have taken the review. It lobbed off the helmet to cover and it was taken by the fielder who charged in and caught it whilst diving. It does not look like it has made any contact with the bat. Let's see. Chameera bends his back and goes short at the bodyline of the batter. The ball kisses off the deck and goes over the bat on the attempted pull from Fakhar. The ball pings the helmet before going towards cover but the UltraEdge shows no bat. Sri Lanka lose an early review.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Dushmantha Chameera to Fakhar Zaman, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On top of off, bowled into the surface, Fakhar gets on top of it and punches it to cover-point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Dushmantha Chameera to Fakhar Zaman, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: How about that for a start? At 139.9 kph, nipping away off the deck with a bit of extra bounce. Fakhar Zaman waits back and gets squared up as the ball zips past the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Dushmantha Chameera to Fakhar Zaman, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Dushmantha Chameera will bowl from the other end.
Shaping away, outside off, full in length. Farhan's feet are rooted in the crease and goes for the drive with his hands. The ball stays low and rolls off the toe end of the bat in front of mid on.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Nuwan Thushara to Sahibzada Farhan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Low full toss, on middle, knocked wide of mid on for a single by Zaman.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Nuwan Thushara to Fakhar Zaman, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Nails the yorker and it tails back into the left-hander. Zaman's head falls over to the off side, but he manages to get some bat on it. Squeezes out an inside edge onto the boot.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Nuwan Thushara to Fakhar Zaman, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: It would have been interesting had the throw hit! Fuller and drifting onto the pads. Fakhar brings his wrists into play and clips it to the right of deep backward square leg. Wanindu Hasaranga is quick across the turf in the deep and fires in a throw on the bounce towards the bowling end. Farhan seemed to be struggling to make his ground but surprisingly, there is no one up to the stumps at the bowling end to collect the throw. It is backed up by a couple of fielders converging from the off side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Nuwan Thushara to Fakhar Zaman, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Not much swing on offer for Thushara. On a good length, on off. Fakhar tentatively hangs his bat out away from his body to block. Gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Nuwan Thushara to Fakhar Zaman, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Sahibzada Farhan and Pakistan are away in the chase! Nuwan sprays it on the pads, on a length. The ball seems to stop on Farhan and he checks his shot. Works it to the right of mid on for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Nuwan Thushara to Sahibzada Farhan, 1 run.
